title: Building big strings fast
description:
Write two functions that build long strings with a table and `table.concat`, never with `..` in a loop:

- `numbers_csv(n)` returns `"1,2,3,...,n"` (an empty string for `n` below 1);
- `repeat_line(word, times, sep)` returns `word` repeated `times` times with `sep` between, like `string.rep(word, times, sep)` but written yourself.

The tests build strings of 200,000 pieces, which takes far too long with `s = s .. piece`.

starter.solution.lua:
function numbers_csv(n)
    local s = ""
    for i = 1, n do
        if i > 1 then s = s .. "," end
        s = s .. i
    end
    return s
end

function repeat_line(word, times, sep)
    local s = ""
    for i = 1, times do s = s .. (i > 1 and sep or "") .. word end
    return s
end

hints: Put each piece in a list and join them once: `table.concat(parts, ",")` (lesson 8.05).
`table.concat` accepts numbers as well as strings, so `parts[i] = i` is enough.
unitTests:
test("small cases", function()
    check_eq(numbers_csv(5), "1,2,3,4,5")
    check_eq(numbers_csv(0), "")
    check_eq(repeat_line("ab", 3, "-"), "ab-ab-ab")
    check_eq(repeat_line("x", 0, ","), "")
    check_eq(repeat_line("x", 2), "xx")
end)

test("200,000 pieces quickly", function()
    local start = os.clock()
    local s = numbers_csv(200000)
    check_eq(#s, 1288894)
    check_eq(s:sub(-13), "199999,200000")
    local r = repeat_line("word", 200000, " ")
    check_eq(#r, 999999)
    check(os.clock() - start < 1, "took too long")
end)
